title: Judges Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 16.

questions.question: Where did Samson go when he saw a harlot and went in unto her?
questions.correctAnswer: Gaza
questions.explanation: Judges 16:1 states that Samson went to Gaza and saw a harlot there and went in unto her.

questions.question: What did the Gazites do when they heard Samson had come to Gaza?
options: They compassed him and laid wait for him all night
They welcomed him into the city
questions.correctAnswer: They compassed him and laid wait for him all night
questions.explanation: Judges 16:2 says the Gazites compassed Samson and laid wait for him all night in the gate of the city.

questions.question: What did Samson do at midnight in Gaza?
options: He took the doors of the gate of the city and carried them upon his shoulders
questions.correctAnswer: He took the doors of the gate of the city and carried them upon his shoulders
questions.explanation: Judges 16:3 recounts that Samson arose at midnight, took the doors of the gate and the two posts, and carried them on his shoulders to a hill before Hebron.

questions.question: What was the name of the woman Samson loved in the valley of Sorek?
questions.correctAnswer: Delilah
questions.explanation: Judges 16:4 clearly states that Samson loved a woman named Delilah in the valley of Sorek.

questions.question: What did the lords of the Philistines offer Delilah to entice Samson?
options: Eleven hundred pieces of silver each
questions.correctAnswer: Eleven hundred pieces of silver each
questions.explanation: Judges 16:5 says the lords of the Philistines promised Delilah eleven hundred pieces of silver each to entice Samson and find out the source of his strength.

questions.question: What did Delilah ask Samson to tell her?
options: Wherein his great strength lieth and wherewith he might be bound
questions.correctAnswer: Wherein his great strength lieth and wherewith he might be bound
questions.explanation: Judges 16:6 records Delilah asking Samson to tell her where his great strength lies and how he might be bound to afflict him.

questions.question: According to Samson, what would make him weak and as another man?
options: Being bound with seven green withs that were never dried
Being tied with chains of iron
questions.correctAnswer: Being bound with seven green withs that were never dried
questions.explanation: Judges 16:7 states Samson told Delilah that if bound with seven green withs that were never dried, he would be weak and like another man.

questions.question: What happened when Delilah bound Samson with the seven green withs?
options: He broke them as a thread of tow is broken when touched by fire
He remained bound and was captured
questions.correctAnswer: He broke them as a thread of tow is broken when touched by fire
questions.explanation: Judges 16:9 describes how Samson broke the seven green withs as a thread of tow is broken when it toucheth the fire, so his strength was not known.

questions.question: True or False: Delilah accused Samson of mocking her and telling lies after the first attempt to bind him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 16:10 records Delilah saying Samson mocked her and told lies after he broke the first binding of green withs.

questions.question: What did Samson say would make him weak the second time Delilah asked?
options: If bound fast with new ropes that never were occupied
If he was chained with brass fetters
If he was put to sleep
questions.correctAnswer: If bound fast with new ropes that never were occupied
questions.explanation: Judges 16:11 states Samson said that if bound with new ropes never used before, he would be weak and like another man.

questions.question: True or False: Samson broke the new ropes that Delilah used to bind him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 16:12 explains that Samson broke the new ropes from off his arms like a thread.

questions.question: What did Samson say would cause him to be weak on the third attempt?
options: If the seven locks of his head were woven with the web
If he was bound with brass fetters
If he was shut in a dark chamber
If he was put to sleep
questions.correctAnswer: If the seven locks of his head were woven with the web
questions.explanation: Judges 16:13 states Samson told Delilah that if she wove the seven locks of his head with the web, he would be weak.

questions.question: What did Delilah do while Samson was asleep on her lap?
options: She called a man to shave off the seven locks of his head
She tied him up with chains
questions.correctAnswer: She called a man to shave off the seven locks of his head
questions.explanation: Judges 16:19 describes Delilah making Samson sleep on her knees and calling a man to shave off the seven locks of his head.

questions.question: In Judges 16, which event comes first?
options: Samson carries the gates of Gaza on his shoulders
Delilah asks Samson about his strength
Samson is captured by the Philistines
The Philistines offer Delilah silver to betray Samson
questions.correctAnswer: Samson carries the gates of Gaza on his shoulders
questions.explanation: Judges 16:3 shows Samson carrying the gates of Gaza first, before Delilah's involvement begins in verse 4 and after.

questions.question: True or False: Samson’s strength left him immediately after Delilah cut his hair.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 16:19-20 states that after Delilah had his hair shaved, his strength went from him and the LORD departed from him.

medium.title: Judges Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Delilah do after Samson told her the secret of his strength?
options: She immediately fled the valley of Sorek
She sent for the lords of the Philistines and received money from them
She warned Samson to flee the Philistines
She told Samson to pray to the Lord for strength
questions.correctAnswer: She sent for the lords of the Philistines and received money from them
questions.explanation: Judges 16:17-18 show that after Samson revealed his secret, Delilah called the lords of the Philistines and received money from them, demonstrating betrayal.

questions.question: How does Judges 16 teach about the danger of not guarding one's heart and secrets?
options: It shows that keeping secrets is always rewarded
It warns that revealing vital secrets can lead to one's downfall
It encourages sharing secrets with everyone
It suggests that strength is unrelated to secrets
questions.correctAnswer: It warns that revealing vital secrets can lead to one's downfall
questions.explanation: Verses 16:17-19 illustrate that when Samson disclosed his secret about his strength to Delilah, she betrayed him, leading to his capture, teaching the importance of guarding one's heart and secrets.

questions.question: What was Samson's condition after Delilah had the seven locks of his head shaved?
options: His strength left him and he was afflicted
He escaped and defeated the Philistines
He went into hiding in the valley of Sorek
questions.correctAnswer: His strength left him and he was afflicted
questions.explanation: Judges 16:19 explains that after his hair was shaved, Samson's strength left him and he was afflicted, showing the connection between his Nazarite vow and his strength.

questions.question: Based on Judges 16:20-21, what happened to Samson after the Philistines captured him?
options: He was crowned king of Gaza
They put out his eyes, bound him with brass fetters, and made him grind in prison
He was released after paying a ransom
He escaped and returned to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They put out his eyes, bound him with brass fetters, and made him grind in prison
questions.explanation: Verses 16:20-21 record that the Philistines blinded Samson, bound him, and forced him to grind in prison, reflecting consequences of his loss of strength after betrayal.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 16:22, Samson's hair began to grow again after he was shaven.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 16:22 states that Samson's hair began to grow again, indicating the potential for restoration of his strength.

questions.question: What reason did Samson give for his great strength in Judges 16:17?
options: He was blessed with strength because of his diet
He was a Nazarite dedicated to God from birth and had never been shaved
He trained extensively as a warrior
He inherited strength from his father
questions.correctAnswer: He was a Nazarite dedicated to God from birth and had never been shaved
questions.explanation: Judges 16:17 explains that Samson's strength derived from his Nazarite vow and uncut hair, showing the connection between obedience to God and strength.

questions.question: How does Judges 16:16-17 teach about the power of persistent temptation and its effect on the soul?
options: It shows that temptation always leads to immediate sin
It highlights how constant pressure can vex and weaken a person's resolve
It teaches that temptation is easily overcome without struggle
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights how constant pressure can vex and weaken a person's resolve
questions.explanation: Verses 16:16-17 describe how Delilah's daily pressing vexed Samson’s soul unto death, causing him to reveal his secret, illustrating how persistent temptation can wear down even strong individuals.

questions.question: What did Delilah say to Samson when he awoke after his hair was cut (Judges 16:20)?
questions.correctAnswer: The Philistines be upon thee
questions.explanation: Judges 16:20 records Delilah's words to Samson upon awakening him, signaling the Philistines’ impending attack and his loss of God's presence.

questions.question: True or False: Samson knew that the LORD had departed from him after his hair was cut, according to Judges 16:20.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 16:20 explicitly states that Samson did not know the LORD had departed from him after his hair was shaved.

questions.question: What was the setting during Samson's final act of strength in Judges 16:27-30?
options: A great feast and sacrifice to the god Dagon with many Philistines present
A secret cave where Samson hid
The valley of Sorek during a quiet afternoon
questions.correctAnswer: A great feast and sacrifice to the god Dagon with many Philistines present
questions.explanation: Judges 16:23-27 describe a large gathering of Philistines at a sacrifice to Dagon where Samson was brought out to entertain, setting the scene for his final act of strength.

questions.question: How does Judges 16:28 teach about humility and reliance on God in times of weakness?
options: Samson arrogantly trusted his own strength alone
Samson called on the LORD to remember and strengthen him for vengeance
Samson ignored God and focused on his enemies
Samson relied on weapons and allies
questions.correctAnswer: Samson called on the LORD to remember and strengthen him for vengeance
questions.explanation: In Judges 16:28, Samson humbly prays to God to renew his strength, showing dependence on God even after failure and weakness.

questions.question: What was the outcome of Samson's final prayer and act of strength in Judges 16:30?
options: He escaped and lived in exile
He died along with many Philistines when the temple collapsed
He was forgiven and released by the Philistines
He defeated the Philistines without harm
questions.correctAnswer: He died along with many Philistines when the temple collapsed
questions.explanation: Judges 16:30 records Samson's death as he pulled down the temple pillars, killing himself and many Philistines, emphasizing sacrificial vengeance and final victory.

questions.question: According to Judges 16:12-14, what happened when Delilah first bound Samson with the seven locks woven into the web and fastened with a pin?
options: Samson awoke and broke free by removing the pin and web
questions.correctAnswer: Samson awoke and broke free by removing the pin and web
questions.explanation: Verses 16:13-14 describe how Delilah bound Samson with his hair woven into a web with a pin, but he awoke and escaped by removing them, showing his continued strength before revealing his secret.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 16:15 shows Delilah accusing Samson of not truly loving her because his heart was not with her.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 16:15 records Delilah confronting Samson, questioning his love because he had mocked her and not revealed the source of his strength, indicating her frustration and distrust.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the lesson about integrity and honesty from Judges 16:10-12?
options: Samson's repeated lying to Delilah protected him completely
Deception can delay consequences but may also lead to greater vulnerability
It is best to deceive those who seek your weakness
questions.correctAnswer: Deception can delay consequences but may also lead to greater vulnerability
questions.explanation: Judges 16:10-12 show Samson lying to Delilah about his strength, which delayed capture but ultimately his deception led to greater vulnerability when he finally revealed the truth.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 16.

questions.question: What was the reason the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon?
options: They had conquered Israel in battle
Their god had delivered Samson into their hand
They wanted to celebrate a harvest festival
They were seeking forgiveness for past sins
questions.correctAnswer: Their god had delivered Samson into their hand
questions.explanation: Judges 16:23 states that the lords of the Philistines gathered to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon because they said, 'Our god hath delivered Samson our enemy into our hand.'

questions.question: How did the people react when they saw Samson during the Philistine celebration?
options: They praised their god for delivering Samson
questions.correctAnswer: They praised their god for delivering Samson
questions.explanation: According to Judges 16:24, when the people saw Samson, they praised their god, saying their god had delivered their enemy and destroyer into their hands.

questions.question: What did the Philistines request Samson to do during their feast?
questions.correctAnswer: Make sport for them
questions.explanation: Judges 16:25 states that the Philistines called for Samson to make sport for them during their feast, setting him between the pillars.

questions.question: What did Samson ask the lad holding his hand before bringing down the house?
options: To let him feel the pillars that support the house
questions.correctAnswer: To let him feel the pillars that support the house
questions.explanation: Judges 16:26 shows that Samson asked the lad to let him feel the pillars upon which the house stood so he might lean upon them.

questions.question: Approximately how many men and women were on the roof watching Samson make sport?
questions.correctAnswer: About 3,000
questions.explanation: Judges 16:27 mentions that about three thousand men and women were on the roof watching while Samson made sport.

questions.question: What did Samson do immediately before bringing down the house upon the Philistines?
options: He prayed to the LORD for strength
questions.correctAnswer: He prayed to the LORD for strength
questions.explanation: In Judges 16:28, Samson called unto the LORD, asking Him to remember and strengthen him so he could take vengeance on the Philistines.

questions.question: How did Samson bring down the Philistine temple?
options: By pulling down the two middle pillars
questions.correctAnswer: By pulling down the two middle pillars
questions.explanation: Judges 16:29 explains that Samson took hold of the two middle pillars supporting the house and pulled them down, causing the house to fall.

questions.question: What was the result of Samson's final act of pulling down the temple?
options: Only the Philistine lords were killed
The dead he slew at his death were more than those slain in his life
questions.correctAnswer: The dead he slew at his death were more than those slain in his life
questions.explanation: Judges 16:30 states that more people died from the collapse than the number Samson killed during his lifetime.

questions.question: Where was Samson buried after his death?
questions.correctAnswer: Between Zorah and Eshtaol
questions.explanation: Judges 16:31 tells that Samson was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol in the burying place of Manoah his father.

questions.question: How long did Samson judge Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: 20 years
questions.explanation: Judges 16:31 concludes by stating that Samson judged Israel for twenty years.

questions.question: Which earlier Scripture passage echoes the theme of God empowering a judge to deliver Israel like Samson in Judges 16?
questions.correctAnswer: Judges 13:5
questions.explanation: Judges 13:5 prophesies Samson will begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines, connecting to his story and final act in Judges 16 where God empowers him one last time.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word 'Nazarite' as used in Judges 16:17 concerning Samson?
options: A person consecrated to God by a vow
questions.correctAnswer: A person consecrated to God by a vow
questions.explanation: Judges 16:17 describes Samson as a Nazarite, meaning he was consecrated to God from birth by a special vow, which included not cutting his hair as a symbol of his dedication.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Judges 16:30 when Samson asks to die with the Philistines?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The narrative forms an inclusio by starting and ending Samson’s story with his strength and death, framing his life and final act in Judges 16:30 with this literary device.

questions.question: True or False: Samson’s hair began to grow again after it was shaved off by the Philistines.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 16:22 states that after Samson was shaved, his hair began to grow again, indicating a restoration of his Nazarite vow symbol.

questions.question: True or False: Samson was immediately aware that the LORD had departed from him after his hair was shaved.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 16:20 clearly states that Samson did not know the LORD had departed from him after his hair was shaved.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Samson carrying away the gates of Gaza in Judges 16:3 reveal about human strength and divine empowerment?
options: Human strength alone enables great feats
Divine empowerment enables Samson's superhuman strength
Physical strength is irrelevant to God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: Divine empowerment enables Samson's superhuman strength
questions.explanation: Judges 16:3 shows Samson carrying the city gates, a feat beyond natural human strength, demonstrating divine empowerment enabling him to carry out God's purposes (cf. Exodus 15:6 for God's enabling power).

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by Samson's Nazarite vow as explained in Judges 16:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of sanctification by separation
questions.explanation: Judges 16:17 explains Samson's strength was tied to his Nazarite vow of separation to God, illustrating sanctification as being set apart for God's service (cf. Numbers 6:1-21).

questions.question: How does the interaction between Delilah and Samson in Judges 16:5-6 and 16:11-12 collectively illustrate human vulnerability to temptation despite divine calling?
options: Divine calling makes one immune to temptation
Human vulnerability persists despite divine calling
Temptation is irrelevant to spiritual strength
Delilah was a divine instrument without human agency
questions.correctAnswer: Human vulnerability persists despite divine calling
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 and 11-12 show Delilah tempting Samson to reveal his weakness, demonstrating that even divinely called individuals retain human vulnerability to sin and temptation.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in Judges 16:20 when Samson awakes and does not realize that the LORD had departed from him?
options: God's justice in withdrawing strength due to sin
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice in withdrawing strength due to sin
questions.explanation: Judges 16:20 demonstrates God's justice in withdrawing His empowering presence from Samson because of his disobedience, reflecting a just and holy God who disciplines sin (cf. Hebrews 12:6).

questions.question: In what way does Samson’s final act in Judges 16:30 typify Christ’s redemptive work?
options: Samson's death is a direct fulfillment of messianic prophecy
Samson’s self-sacrifice brings deliverance to Israel
Samson acts out of revenge and hate
questions.correctAnswer: Samson’s self-sacrifice brings deliverance to Israel
questions.explanation: Judges 16:30 shows Samson sacrificing himself to defeat the Philistines, foreshadowing Christ’s atoning death that brings ultimate deliverance to His people (cf. John 10:18).

questions.question: What theological insight is gained from the fact that Samson’s hair began to grow again after being shaven as stated in Judges 16:22?
options: Hair growth is unrelated to spiritual condition
Samson regained all his previous strength immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Restoration and hope after failure
questions.explanation: Judges 16:22 symbolizes that despite failure and judgment, God’s grace allows restoration and hope, as Samson’s hair—and thus potential strength—began to return.

questions.question: How does Judges 16:23-24 demonstrate the Philistines’ misunderstanding of true divine power?
options: They correctly acknowledge their god’s supremacy
They attribute Samson’s capture to their god instead of the true God
They recognize the LORD’s power over Samson
They repent and turn to the God of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They attribute Samson’s capture to their god instead of the true God
questions.explanation: Verses 23-24 show the Philistines praising Dagon for delivering Samson, revealing their ignorance of the true God’s sovereignty and power.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about strength and human frailty do Judges 16:9 and 16:19 convey?
options: True strength depends on obedience to God
Physical strength is the source of salvation
Delilah’s power is greater than God’s
questions.correctAnswer: True strength depends on obedience to God
questions.explanation: Judges 16:9 shows Samson breaking the withs due to God’s ongoing empowerment, but 16:19 shows loss of strength when his hair is cut and God departs, teaching that true strength depends on God’s presence and obedience.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Judges 16 portrays God as arbitrary in giving and taking Samson’s strength. What does Judges 16:17-20 actually teach about God's justice and holiness?
options: God’s strength is given and taken arbitrarily
God’s withdrawal of strength is a just response to Samson’s disobedience
God is indifferent to human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God’s withdrawal of strength is a just response to Samson’s disobedience
questions.explanation: Verses 17-20 explain that Samson’s strength was contingent on his Nazarite vow and relationship with God; breaking that leads to God justly withdrawing His empowering presence, reflecting His holiness and justice.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Judges 16:31 make between Samson’s judgeship and the broader redemptive history of Israel?
options: Samson’s judgeship represents God’s continued deliverance despite Israel’s failures
Samson’s death ended Israel’s need for deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: Samson’s judgeship represents God’s continued deliverance despite Israel’s failures
questions.explanation: Judges 16:31 notes Samson judged Israel 20 years, showing God’s ongoing mercy to deliver Israel through imperfect leaders despite their repeated sinfulness, fitting the cycle of redemption in Judges.

questions.question: What attribute of God is particularly exemplified in Samson’s prayer for strength in Judges 16:28?
options: God’s mercy and willingness to restore strength
God’s silence in times of distress
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mercy and willingness to restore strength
questions.explanation: Judges 16:28 shows Samson calling on the LORD to remember and strengthen him once more, revealing God’s merciful nature to respond to repentant prayer.

questions.question: How do Judges 16:13-14 and 16:19 together illustrate the consequences of deceit and broken trust in a covenant relationship with God?
options: Broken trust leads to loss of divine favor and strength
Delilah was justified in her actions
God’s covenant is conditional on human strength
questions.correctAnswer: Broken trust leads to loss of divine favor and strength
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 show Samson deceiving Delilah about his strength; 16:19 shows his hair shaved and strength lost, illustrating how deceit and broken trust result in loss of God’s blessing.

questions.question: What does Judges 16:1-2 teach about the consequences of Samson’s personal choices on Israel’s spiritual and national welfare?
options: His choices brought danger to Israel by exposing him to Philistine plots
His actions had no impact on Israel’s enemies
questions.correctAnswer: His choices brought danger to Israel by exposing him to Philistine plots
questions.explanation: Verses 1-2 show Samson’s visit to a harlot in Gaza led to the Philistines plotting to kill him, endangering Israel by exposing their judge to enemy schemes.

questions.question: What synthesis about divine sovereignty and human responsibility emerges from Judges 16:4 and 16:15-16 regarding Samson and Delilah’s relationship?
options: God is not involved in human relationships
Samson’s fall is due solely to Delilah’s deceit
Divine sovereignty permits human sin, but human responsibility remains
Delilah acted under direct divine command
questions.correctAnswer: Divine sovereignty permits human sin, but human responsibility remains
questions.explanation: Verse 4 shows Samson’s love for Delilah, while 15-16 show her pressing him to reveal his secret, illustrating that God’s sovereign plan works through human choices, which carry responsibility.

questions.question: How does Judges 16:25-27 inform our understanding of Israel’s spiritual condition during Samson’s captivity?
options: Israel was faithfully worshiping the LORD
The Philistines were celebrating their gods, showing Israel’s spiritual defeat
Israel was victorious over the Philistines
Samson led Israel in worship during captivity
questions.correctAnswer: The Philistines were celebrating their gods, showing Israel’s spiritual defeat
questions.explanation: Verses 25-27 describe the Philistines holding a festival to their god Dagon, with Israel under Philistine oppression, reflecting Israel’s spiritual and national decline.
